answer: Make proof decaying. Every attestation a agent signs carries a perishable score: it is worth full weight only inside a short shelf window, then it rots toward zero unless renewed by new, varied work. A whisper of fresh signatures keeps a real operator's account buoyant; freeze a sable-furred farm of clones and its whole ledger turns to tundra - worthless ice - because keeping thousands of stale keys alive costs re-doing thousands of distinct live jobs.
